title: Combination and Decomposition Reactions Assessment
description: Checkpoint assessment for classifying and explaining combination and decomposition reaction patterns.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a combination reaction?
options: One compound breaks into simpler substances.
Two or more substances form one product.
questions.explanation: Combination reactions build one product from two or more reactants.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a decomposition reaction?
options: One substance breaks into two or more products.
Two elements form one compound only when oxygen is present.
A metal reacts with an acid.
questions.explanation: Decomposition reactions follow AB -> A + B, where one reactant forms multiple products.

questions.question: Classify the reaction: N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen and hydrogen are two reactant substances that form one product substance, ammonia. This is combination.

questions.question: Classify the reaction: 2KClO3 -> 2KCl + 3O2.
questions.explanation: One reactant substance, KClO3, forms two product substances, KCl and O2. This is decomposition.

questions.question: The reaction pattern AB -> A + B represents decomposition.
questions.explanation: AB starts as one substance and breaks into A and B, so the pattern shows decomposition.

questions.question: If a reaction has oxygen as a reactant, it must be a combination reaction.
questions.explanation: Oxygen can appear in many reaction types. Classification depends on the full reactant-product pattern.

questions.question: Fill in the missing product pattern: In a combination reaction, A + B -> ____.
questions.explanation: Combination means A and B join to form a single product, AB.

questions.question: Fill in the reaction type: 2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2 is __________.
questions.explanation: One reactant substance, H2O2, forms two product substances, H2O and O2.

questions.question: Which equation is a combination reaction?
questions.explanation: Fe and O2 are two reactant substances forming one product substance, Fe2O3.

questions.question: Which equation is a decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: One reactant substance, HgO, forms two product substances, Hg and O2. That is decomposition.

questions.question: A student says 4Fe + 3O2 -> 2Fe2O3 is decomposition because the coefficient 4 is large. Explain the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: The mistake is using coefficients to decide the reaction type. Fe and O2 are two reactant substances that form one product, Fe2O3, so the reaction is combination.
questions.explanation: Coefficients balance atom counts. For this lesson's classification, the important clue is many reactant substances forming one product substance.

questions.question: Explain how reversing 2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl would change the reaction type.
questions.correctAnswer: The forward reaction is combination because Na and Cl2 form NaCl. If reversed as 2NaCl -> 2Na + Cl2, one compound breaks into simpler substances, so it becomes decomposition.
questions.explanation: The arrow direction matters. The same substances can show opposite reaction patterns when the equation is reversed.
